finding_summary: Borrower has failed to pay 5 consecutive monthly installments from April 2025 through August 2025 totaling INR 1,62,50,000 in scheduled EMIs, together with accrued and penal interest. The first payment default occurred on 2025-04-01 and remains uncured as of 2025-08-31.
Total outstanding exposure as of 2025-08-31 is INR 12,40,00,000 comprising principal outstanding of INR 12,00,00,000, accrued interest of INR 37,30,000, and penal interest of INR 2,70,000.
Three securities documented: (a) property mortgage; (b) corporate guarantee; (c) receivables charge. All appear properly documented pending verification of registration certificates and title deeds.

Last property valuation dated 2024-02 (pre-disbursement). Current market value unknown. Property values in Andheri-Kurla Road area may have appreciated 15-20% since 2024, but this requires confirmation.

Last audited financials available: FY2023-24. FY2024-25 financials not yet available. Borrower's current financial position and solvency status cannot be definitively assessed without updated financials.

Optimal recovery pathway (SARFAESI vs. DRT vs. IBC) requires legal judgment based on: security enforceability, borrower solvency, asset valuation, timeline, costs, and recovery likelihood. Cannot be determined without external counsel advice.
Title and security records identify a mortgage created in 2014 in favour of Zenith Commercial Bank Limited over AST-001.
A 2019 release letter indicates repayment and release intent, but the available dataset does not contain conclusive registration evidence establishing formal satisfaction of the 2014 mortgage.

Current security records identify Aster Fintech Limited's 2024 mortgage over AST-001. This supports existence of the lender's claimed security, subject to counsel verification of priority and enforceability.

finding_title: Security Issue May Affect Recovery Strategy
finding_summary: The unresolved historical mortgage record could affect recovery strategy or sequencing. MatterBridge cannot determine legal priority or enforceability from the available documents and external counsel review is required.
Submitted medical documents contain inconsistent facility, doctor or patient identifiers. These inconsistencies support further verification but do not establish intentional falsification.
HR records show 17 unscheduled absence days, five notification-process failures and prior attendance interventions during the preceding 12 months.
The employee achieved 77/100 against the stated passing threshold of 75/100. Historical performance concerns therefore should not be represented as a failed PIP.

finding_title: Leave and Misconduct Analysis Should Remain Separate
finding_summary: The leave request, prior attendance history and current document-authenticity investigation involve different evidence and legal considerations. Combining them into a single misconduct conclusion would exceed the available evidence.

Complete document verification and obtain Legal review before linking the current leave request to disciplinary action. Any decision should distinguish verified misconduct evidence from historical performance records and leave-related rights.
